guides-filter-media.s67: Send us the filter type and tank size — we’ll recommend the optimal order

guides-eco-friendly.s3: Your all‑in‑one guide to turning your tank from just glass and water into a thriving, sustainable ecosystem. We cover the basics, maintenance, and troubleshooting.
guides-eco-friendly.s10: The Nitrogen Cycle: The Heart of the Tank
guides-eco-friendly.s12: Don’t put fish in right away!
guides-eco-friendly.s13: The tank needs "cycling" to build beneficial bacteria that break down toxic fish waste. Without this cycle, fish may die from ammonia poisoning.
guides-eco-friendly.s21: Ensure the filter and pump are working
guides-eco-friendly.s23: Feed an appropriate amount (eaten within two minutes)
guides-eco-friendly.s26: Clean the tank glass from the inside
guides-eco-friendly.s29: Wash the filter sponge (using only tank water)

guides-filter-choice.s56: Check water flow — if low, the sponge needs cleaning
guides-filter-choice.s58: Clean the sponge with tank water, not bleach — to preserve beneficial bacteria
guides-filter-choice.s60: Inspect the motor and fans — deep clean the external filter
guides-filter-choice.s62: Do not clean the filter and change the water on the same day — it shocks beneficial bacteria
guides-filter-choice.s63: Not sure which filter suits your tank?
guides-filter-choice.s64: Send us the tank size and number of fish — we’ll guide you to the best option within your budget.

guides-quarantine.s4: Two weeks to protect the entire tank from one disease
guides-quarantine.s5: A quarantine tank is not a luxury — it’s essential for anyone adding new fish. One sick fish without quarantine can spread disease to the entire tank within days.
guides-quarantine.s8: What you need for a simple quarantine tank
guides-quarantine.s10: 10–20 liters is enough for most small fish. No need for a large volume.
guides-quarantine.s12: Place it in the main tank a week before use to activate bacteria
guides-quarantine.s14: Maintain the same temperature as the main tank — a difference adds stress
guides-quarantine.s16: The sick or nervous fish jumps. A cover protects and reduces stress
guides-quarantine.s20: Add fish slowly — gradually mix water over 30 minutes. Monitor breathing and movement
guides-quarantine.s23: Check daily: spots, symptoms, appetite. If anything appears — start treatment immediately

guides-feeding-table.s5: Overfeeding spoils the water faster than anything else
guides-feeding-table.s6: The golden rule: what the fish eat in two minutes is the limit. Anything left in the water breaks down, raises ammonia, and destroys the biological cycle.
guides-feeding-table.s9: The right amount based on fish size
guides-feeding-table.s10: There is no fixed gram amount – the rule is two minutes. The fish size determines how many pellets to start with.
guides-feeding-table.s19: Larger pellets suitable for mouth size
guides-feeding-table.s24: Observe over two minutes – what remains = what was eaten
guides-feeding-table.s25: The right timing – when to feed?
guides-feeding-table.s28: One hour after lights on – fish are more active and ready
guides-feeding-table.s31: Two hours before lights off – enough time for digestion before sleep
guides-feeding-table.s34: Fish are asleep and food breaks down in the water all night – harmful with no benefit
guides-feeding-table.s35: How do you know you’re overfeeding?
guides-feeding-table.s36: These signs appear before you see any fish affected:
guides-feeding-table.s38: Bacterial growth from leftover food – a clear sign of overfeeding
guides-feeding-table.s40: Food rots on the bottom or in the gravel
guides-feeding-table.s42: Food residue raises nitrates – algae fuel

guides-aquarium-salt.s37: ⚠ Salt does not evaporate with water—it accumulates. With each water change, add only the amount needed for the changed volume, not the entire tank.
guides-aquarium-salt.s38: Not sure of the right amount for your tank?
guides-aquarium-salt.s39: Send us your tank size and fish type—and we’ll calculate it accurately for you.

guides-treatment-basics.s3: The wrong medicine kills faster than the disease itself
guides-treatment-basics.s4: Most treatment failures stem from medication without proper diagnosis, incorrect dosage, or water neglect. These four steps protect your fish before you open any bottle.
guides-treatment-basics.s10: External signs (spots, color, behavior) determine the problem type. Bacterial? Fungal? Parasitic? Each type requires a different medicine. The wrong medicine stresses the liver and weakens the fish’s natural defenses.
guides-treatment-basics.s11: Send a clear photo—visual diagnosis is more accurate than guessing.
guides-treatment-basics.s14: Before adding any medicine to the main tank—isolating the sick fish protects the rest and gives you better control over dose and duration.
guides-treatment-basics.s15: Exception: if ich or parasites have spread—the entire tank needs treatment.
guides-treatment-basics.s17: Read the instructions fully—don’t just skim
guides-treatment-basics.s18: Dose based on tank size. Full duration (do not stop if the fish improves). The medicine’s effect on the biological filter and oxygen.
guides-treatment-basics.s19: Some medicines require removing activated carbon and dimming the lights.
guides-treatment-basics.s22: After the treatment period ends—replace 30 % of the water to remove drug residues. Keep activated carbon for an extra week to ensure drug removal.
guides-treatment-basics.s23: Observe the fish for 48 hours after treatment before returning it to the main tank.
guides-treatment-basics.s24: Mistakes that kill fish during treatment
guides-treatment-basics.s25: Increasing the dose "to speed up treatment"
guides-treatment-basics.s26: A dose double the recommendation poisons the liver and kidneys—killing the fish instead of healing it
guides-treatment-basics.s27: Stopping treatment early because the fish "improves"
guides-treatment-basics.s28: Symptoms disappear before the disease is eradicated—early cessation creates resistance
guides-treatment-basics.s29: Mixing different medicines at the same time
guides-treatment-basics.s30: Unexpected chemical reactions—and sometimes lethal outcomes
guides-treatment-basics.s31: Treating fish without checking water quality
guides-treatment-basics.s32: High ammonia weakens the immune system—any treatment will fail with it
